title: East Moor (near Sutton-on-the-Forest) served Memorial
inscription:
BASE, FRONT FACE: THIS MEMORIAL IS DEDICATED TO ALL WHO SERVED AT EASTMOOR
IN WORLD WAR II. MANY OF WHOM GAVE THEIR LIVES AND IN
GRATITUDE TO THE PEOPLE OF YORKSHIRE WHO WELCOMED THEM. BASE, REAR FACE: ERECTED BY THEIR FAMILIES AND FORMER COLLEAGUES
DEDICATED THIS 2ND DAY OF JUNE 1990 FORTUNAE NIHIL
NOV 1942 - AUG 1943 BASE, RIGHT FACE: SAEVITER AD LUCEM
SEP 1943 - MAY 1945 BASE, LEFT FACE: AD METUM
JULY 1944 - MAY 1945 Base of Gnomen: RAF EASTMOOR 54, 04'N 01.05'W
Squadrons: 429 Squadron, 415 Squadron, 432 Squadron
memorial_type: Airfield memorial near site of former East Moor airfield

title: Faldingworth — 300 Polish Squadron Memorial
inscription:
300 SQN POLISH AIR FORCE
1944-1947
1667 HCU RAF 1943
TO THOSE WHO WHEN TYRANNY THREATENED

SOME NEVER TO RETURN

title: Fiskerton — St Clement's Church, 49 Squadron Memorial
Great Steeping — 207 Squadron Memorial Plaque, All Saints Church
inscription: 511 men of 207 Squadron killed October 1943 to October 1945 from RAF Spilsby. 104 have no known grave. Nationalities: Great Britain, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, United States, Netherlands, Eire. Also 12 ground staff.

title: Kirmington — 166 Squadron Memorial Garden
inscription:
YE THAT LIVE ON MID ENGLAND'S PASTURES GREEN
THINK ON US AND WHAT MIGHT HAVE BEEN
THIS MEMORIAL IS DEDICATED TO ALL THE MEN AND WOMEN WHO SERVED WITH 166 SQUADRON
AT ROYAL AIR FORCE KIRMINGTON 1943-1945
OF WHOM 921 GAVE THEIR LIVES THAT WE MIGHT BE FREE

inscription: This Plinth was donated by former members of 75 NEW ZEALAND SQUADRON R.A.F. stationed at Mepal between 1943 and 1945 IN REMEMBRANCE OF THOSE WHO FAILED TO RETURN

title: RAF East Kirkby, Station Ground Crew
inscription: THIS MEMORIAL IS DEDICATED TO ALL THE OFFICERS,/ N.C.O.’s, AIRMEN AND AIRWOMEN OF THE GROUND CREWS / / GROUND STAFF WHO SERVED WITH 57 AND 630 LANCASTER/ SQUADRONS AT EAST KIRKBY DURING 1943 – 45./ PRESENTED IN GRATEFUL MEMORY BY THE 57 AND 630/ SQUADRONS ASSOCIATION AND UNVEILED BY IT’S/ PRESIDENT./ SIR IVOR BROOM KCB, CBE, DSO, DFC**, AFC. ON THE/ 11th JULY 1999/ Three Cheers for the Man on the Ground/ Wherever you walk, you will hear people talk,/ Of the men who go up in the air,/ Of the daredevil way, they go into the fray;/ Facing death without turning a hair./ They'll raise a big cheer and buy lots of beer,/ For a pilot who's home on leave;/ But they don't give a jigger/ For a flight mech or riggcr/ With nothing but 'props on his sleeve./ They just say 'Nice day' and then turn away,/ With never a mention of praise./ And the poor bloody erk, who does all the work;/ Just orders his own beer/ And pays!/ They've never been told of the hours in the cold/ That he spends sealing Germany's fate./ How he works on a kite, till all hours of the night;/ And then turns up next morning at eight./ He gets no rake-off, for working till take-off;/ Or helping the aircrew prepare;/ But whenever there's trouble, it's 'Quick at the double';/ The man on the ground must be there./ Each flying crew could tell it to you;/ They know what this man's really worth./ They know that he's part of the RAF's heart,/ Even though he stays close to the earth./ He doesn't want glory, but please tell his story;/ Spread a little of his fame around./ He's one of a few so give him his due;/ Three Cheers for the man on the ground./ Eric Sykes 1942
